operations.evidence: The quarterly release covers use of police powers under terrorism and subsequent legislation in Great Britain up to the year ending 31 March 2026.
The release is a national or jurisdictional aggregate and cannot identify risk at an individual parcel.
The release also covers arrests for terrorist-related activity made under other legislation, including the Police and Criminal Evidence Act.
An arrest category does not establish guilt or parcel-level conditions.
Administrative data are updated as cases progress through the criminal justice system, so figures may be revised in future releases.
Recent outcome counts are provisional and must not be treated as fixed parcel evidence.
Arrest and outcome data reflect the latest case position supplied by the Counter Terrorism Policing Headquarters Coordination Centre on 5 May 2026.
Later case developments may change charges, prosecutions and convictions.
There were 3,061 arrests for terrorism-related activity in the year ending 31 March 2026.
This is a Great Britain total and not a neighbourhood incident count.
The 3,061 arrests represented a 1,186% increase compared with 238 in the previous year.
The increase is dominated by a specific legal and operational context and cannot be extrapolated to parcels.
There were 2,819 arrests linked to supporting Palestine Action after its proscription on 5 July 2025.
This aggregate must not be used to infer beliefs, conduct or risk for individuals or locations.
Palestine Action-linked arrests represented 92% of the 3,061 terrorism-related arrests.
The share reflects the release's classification and does not measure general local terrorism risk.
After excluding Palestine Action-linked arrests, there were 242 terrorism-related arrests.
The residual category remains a national aggregate and is not parcel evidence.
The 242 other terrorism-related arrests were 1.7% higher than the previous year's 238.
Small national changes do not support exact-address scoring.
Of the 242 other arrests, 44 occurred from January to March 2026.
Quarterly national counts cannot be spatially attributed to a parcel.
The 44 other arrests in January to March 2026 were 32% lower than the 65 in October to December 2025.
Quarter-to-quarter volatility does not establish a local trend.
At the data cutoff, 551 arrests, or 18%, had resulted in a charge.
The charge rate can increase as unresolved cases progress.
The total charges included 484 arrests linked to supporting Palestine Action.
Charges are allegations and must not be treated as convictions or parcel risk.
There were 41 arrests of individuals aged 17 and under, including one linked to supporting Palestine Action.
Age-group statistics must not be used to profile individuals or places.
Among non-Palestine Action arrests where age was known, 40 of 241, or 17%, involved individuals aged 17 and under.
The denominator excludes unknown ages and the statistic is not a local rate.
The 17% share of minors among non-Palestine Action arrests was down from 19% in the year ending March 2025.
Year-to-year demographic shares are not parcel-level evidence.
Seventy-two persons were tried for terrorism-related offences in the year ending 31 March 2026.
Trial counts are based on completed court cases and cannot be mapped to an address.
Of the 72 persons tried, 67 were convicted.
Conviction counts are England and Wales court aggregates, not parcel indicators.
The conviction rate among the 72 trials was 93%.
The rate is conditional on cases reaching trial and does not describe all arrests.
